payload.name: Preserve distinct facts when updating memories
payload.description: When updating an existing memory with new unrelated information, check the previous version and keep all still-true facts that are not contradicted; if necessary, MERGE or ADD instead of replacing the whole memory.
content: Before applying UPDATE to an existing memory, compare the candidate content with the previous version.

If new content covers different events or attributes and does not contradict the old content, preserve the old facts in the merged memory or keep the old memory unchanged and ADD the new facts as a separate memory.
Only drop a prior fact if new evidence explicitly contradicts it; do not delete old facts merely because the new message is more recent or appears to be a replacement.
When merging, combine related facts concisely while retaining each distinct claim and its source/session.

solves: During construction, a later UPDATE can overwrite an earlier correctly stored memory with unrelated new facts, making the reference answer unrecoverable. This rule generalizes to any future session where an enrichment update touches a memory containing other still-valid claims: preserve distinct facts unless explicitly contradicted, using MERGE/ADD instead of replacement. It does not apply when new evidence directly supersedes or contradicts the old fact.
